2027-06-01.title: Third Tuesday of the Apostles · St Justin, Martyr
2027-06-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The kingdom of God is not in talk but in power
Do not put a stumbling block before the little ones
2027-06-01.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), from Pentecost to the beginning of the Season of Summer (Kaitha): the Church remembers the apostles who, filled with the Holy Spirit, preached Christ and founded the Churches, among them the Church of India founded by Mar Thoma. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed at the three hours of the day. St Justin, martyr: Genesis 18:23–32; Wisdom 10:9–14; 1 Corinthians 1:18–25; Luke 12:2–8. In the Latin calendar St Justin is also remembered today.
2027-06-01.verse: For the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.
theo: The first day of June opens with a father's letter. Paul writes to a quarrelsome community he loves, and he does not hide his feelings: “For though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.” The guardian in a Greek household was the slave who walked the children to school and kept an eye on them; he could be strict and useful, but he was not their father. Paul claims something deeper. He did not merely supervise the Corinthians; he begot them in faith by preaching Christ to them. That is why he can say, without pride, “I appeal to you, then, be imitators of me.” Faith is handed on not only by teaching but by a life that can be copied. Paul sends Timothy, “my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, to remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus.” This is the apostolic pattern of the whole Season of the Apostles: a father in the faith, a son trained by him, and a community that learns the ways of Christ by watching those who walk in them. In these days, when schools reopen across Kerala and children set out with new bags and new books, the Church reminds parents, godparents, teachers and priests that they are more than guardians. Children learn the faith first from the way we pray, speak and forgive at home.

Then Paul turns to those who have grown arrogant, thinking that he will never come back: “But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of these arrogant people but their power. For the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.” Corinth loved clever speech. Some had made themselves important by talking well about spiritual things. Paul asks a simple question: what has your talk produced? The kingdom of God is shown by the power of the Spirit that changes lives, heals divisions and makes people holy. Words about God are cheap; a life changed by God is costly and convincing. Then the tender ending: “What would you prefer? Am I to come to you with a stick, or with love in a spirit of gentleness?” A good father can correct, but he would much rather come with gentleness. The choice, Paul says, is partly theirs.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks some of the sternest words he ever spoke, and he speaks them in defence of the little ones: “If any of you put a stumbling block before one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for you if a great millstone were fastened around your neck and you were drowned in the depth of the sea.” The millstone was the heavy stone turned by a donkey to grind grain. Jesus does not use such language lightly. To lead a child, or any simple believer, into sin or out of faith is a grave evil. The Church has had to hear these words with shame in our own time, when some who should have been fathers in the faith harmed the little ones entrusted to them; every parish and institution is bound to protect children and vulnerable people, to listen to them and to act. Then Jesus turns the warning inward: “If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away.” He is not asking for mutilation; he is asking for decisiveness. Whatever in my life leads me into sin, a habit, a company, an app on the phone, must be cut off firmly, because eternal life is worth more than anything we give up.

Today the Church remembers St Justin, one of the first great Christian thinkers. Born in Samaria early in the second century, he searched for the truth among the philosophers of his day, until an old man he met by the sea pointed him to the prophets and to Christ. He became, as he said, a philosopher of the true philosophy, opened a school in Rome, and wrote to the emperor to defend the Christians. In those writings he left the earliest full description of the Sunday Eucharist outside the New Testament: the reading of the memoirs of the apostles and the prophets, the homily, the prayers, the bread and wine brought to the presider, the great thanksgiving, the Amen of the people, and the gifts carried to the absent. Around the year 165 he was arrested with several companions and beheaded under the prefect Rusticus for refusing to sacrifice to the gods. The readings of his feast fit his life: “the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God” (1 Corinthians 1:18), and “everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God” (Luke 12:8). Justin's power was not in talk, though he talked well; it was in the witness of his blood.
outline: A new month and a new school year: who are the fathers and mothers in faith for our children?
Paul begets the Corinthians through the Gospel and sends Timothy to remind them of his ways.
The kingdom is shown by changed lives; a stick or gentleness.
The millstone, the duty to protect, and cutting off what causes sin.
The philosopher who found Christ, described the Sunday Qurbana and died for the faith.
“The kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.”
live: Parents and godparents: pray once this week with your children, aloud and unhurried, so that they can copy what they see.
Know your parish's child-protection guidelines and speak up if a child is in danger.
Name one habit, company or app that leads you into sin, and remove it this week.
fathers: On the day called Sunday all who live in the cities or in the country gather in one place. The memoirs of the apostles or the writings of the prophets are read as long as time permits; the presider exhorts us to imitate these good things; we stand and pray; bread and wine and water are brought, he gives thanks as best he can, and the people say Amen. Then each one receives, and the deacons carry a portion to those who are absent.

Nothing is more precious than a soul. To build up a child in virtue is a greater work than any painter or sculptor can do. Do not say that the child is too young: a young plant is easily bent, and what you teach now will remain.
magis: Parents have the first responsibility for the education of their children; they bear witness to this responsibility first by creating a home where tenderness, forgiveness, respect, fidelity and service are the rule.
Scandal takes on a particular gravity by reason of the authority of those who cause it or the weakness of those who are scandalized; Jesus pronounced a curse on it in Matthew 18:6.
As early as the second century St Justin Martyr gave the basic lines of the order of the Eucharistic celebration, which have stayed the same until our own day.
saints: St Justin (c. 100–c. 165), philosopher and martyr, born at Flavia Neapolis (Nablus) in Samaria, teacher in Rome, author of two Apologies and the Dialogue with Trypho; beheaded with companions under the prefect Junius Rusticus.

1–6 June: the third and fourth weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Tue 1: St Justin, martyr. Thu 3: in the Latin calendar, St Charles Lwanga and his companions, the Martyrs of Uganda. Fri 4: the Feast of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Third Friday of the Apostles), and First Friday. Sat 5: the Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (Third Saturday of the Apostles); in the Latin calendar also St Boniface. Sun 6: Fourth Sunday of the Apostles. June is the month of the Sacred Heart in popular devotion; in Kerala it is also the month the schools reopen and the monsoon rains arrive.
2027-06-01.prayer: Father of all, you gave the Corinthians a father in the faith through the Gospel, and you gave St Justin the wisdom to find in Christ the truth he was seeking. Give our children faithful fathers and mothers, teachers and priests, whose lives they can copy. Keep the little ones from every stumbling block, and give us courage to cut off whatever leads us into sin. Let your kingdom be seen among us not in talk but in the power of your Holy Spirit. Through Christ our Lord, to whom with you and the Holy Spirit be glory for ever. Amen.
altar: St Justin tells us that already in the second century the Christians gathered on Sunday to hear the apostles and prophets, to give thanks over bread and wine, and to say Amen. Every Holy Qurbana is that same gathering, and the Amen we say before Communion is the Amen of Justin and his companions, who sealed it with their blood.

2027-06-01.question: Is my faith more talk than power?

family.explain: Saint Paul says that he is like a father to the Christians in Corinth, because he told them about Jesus. He asks them to copy the way he lives. Jesus says that little children are very precious to God, and that nobody should ever lead a child to do wrong. Grown-ups must protect children, and children must tell a grown-up they trust if anyone makes them feel unsafe.
family.intention: We pray for children starting a new school year, and for their teachers.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we copy in our family, and is it a good example?”

illus: On the first day of the new school year, a headmistress in a government school near Thrissur stood at the gate to greet the children. One small boy arrived crying, clutching his father's hand. The father was embarrassed and tried to push him in. The headmistress knelt down, took out a sweet, and asked the boy what he liked. ‘Drawing,’ he whispered. ‘Then you will draw the first picture on our new classroom wall,’ she said. Twenty years later, when that boy became a teacher himself, he said at his first staff meeting: ‘I do not remember a single lesson from that year. I remember a teacher who knelt down at the gate.’ Children learn first from the way they are treated.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you love the little ones and you want your kingdom to be seen in power, not in empty words. Send your Holy Spirit upon us as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel (1 Corinthians 4:15). Who has been a father or mother in faith to me?
The kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power (1 Corinthians 4:20). Where is my faith only words?
If any of you put a stumbling block before one of these little ones (Matthew 18:6). How do I protect the children around me?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Luke 12:8). When have I been afraid to say that I am a Christian?
pm.resp: Lord, let your kingdom come in power.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that pastors and parents may be true fathers and mothers in faith.
For children beginning the new school year, for their teachers and for all who work in schools.
For children who have been harmed, that they may be heard, protected and healed.
For Christian thinkers, teachers and students, that like St Justin they may seek the truth and find it in Christ.
For Christians who suffer for their faith today.
pm.close: Father, you raised up St Justin to proclaim Christ, the wisdom and power of God. Give us faithful hearts, protect the little ones, and make our lives a witness to your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today Saint Paul writes like a father. He says to the Corinthians: you have many guardians, but not many fathers; I became your father in Christ through the Gospel (1 Corinthians 4:15). Faith is not only taught; it is passed on by people who love us and whose lives we can copy.

This week children go back to school. Let us ask ourselves: who are the fathers and mothers in faith for our children? Not only priests and catechism teachers, but parents, grandparents and godparents. Children learn to pray by watching us pray.

Paul says: the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power (1 Corinthians 4:20). It is easy to talk about God. The real sign of the kingdom is a life changed by the Holy Spirit: a temper calmed, a quarrel healed, a habit broken.

In the Gospel Jesus defends the little ones with strong words: it would be better to have a millstone around one's neck than to lead a little one into sin. Let us protect our children in every way. And let us be firm with ourselves: whatever leads us into sin, let us cut it off.

Today we remember Saint Justin. He searched for the truth among the philosophers, found it in Christ, and gave his life for him in Rome. He also told us how the first Christians celebrated the Eucharist on Sunday. When we say Amen at the Qurbana, we say it with Justin. May our faith, like his, be not only talk but power. Amen.
kids: Children, Saint Paul was like a father to the first Christians, because he told them about Jesus. Who told you about Jesus? Say thank you to them today!
Jesus loves children very much. If anyone ever makes you feel unsafe or asks you to do something wrong, tell your parents or a teacher you trust.

intro: Theme: “For the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.”
A father in the faith, the power of the Spirit that changes lives, the little ones whom Jesus defends, and St Justin, who found the truth in Christ.

q: Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
For though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
points.apply: Pray once this week with a child, slowly and aloud.

q: He said to me, “This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the Lord of hosts.
For the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit each morning this week for one concrete change in your life.

points.h: Woe to the one who causes the little ones to stumble
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak, but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them with justice.

If any of you put a stumbling block before one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for you if a great millstone were fastened around your neck and you were drowned in the depth of the sea.
points.apply: Remove one occasion of sin from your life this week.

concl: The faith is handed on by fathers and mothers whose lives can be copied, and the kingdom is shown in the Spirit's power.
With St Justin, let our Amen be sealed by a life that witnesses to Christ.
2027-06-01.resolve: This week, pray with a child, protect the little ones, and cut off one thing that leads you into sin.
